domain_label: US Fashion/Costume Jewelry — Category Demand Structure & Finish/Tier Segmentation
purpose: A method for reading US fashion/costume jewelry demand by category (earrings/necklaces/rings/bracelets/anklets) and by finish tier (fine vs fashion; solid-gold vs gold-plated/vermeil/gold-filled vs rhodium-plated silver vs stainless/steel), carrying the FTC 16 CFR Part 23 finish definitions as [FACT], encoding the public-data [METHOD]s that size category demand and the [METHOD] that estimates solid-vs-plated share, and stating why fashion/costume is the owner's tier — all without inventing a single market number.
assumptions: no proprietary sales dataset is supplied; every demand quantity is produced by an explicit [METHOD] over public signals (marketplace best-seller ranks, keyword search volume, retail assortment share) and carried as [ESTIMATE] with confidence, never as a measured fact

the FTC Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries (16 CFR Part 23) are the controlling US definitions of gold-plated, gold electroplate, gold-filled/overlay, vermeil, rhodium/platinum-group and sterling-silver marking, cited as [FACT] with the specific micron/karat thresholds flagged for verification against the current published text

the owner's venture is a DTC plated-jewelry line aimed at young women (~18-25), so the fashion/costume tier and the plated/rhodium finish family are the relevant segment; the fine (solid-gold, natural-stone) tier is carried only as the contrast pole, not the target

category and finish are two orthogonal cuts of the same catalog: any category (e.g. hoop earring) exists across the whole finish ladder, so demand must be read on both axes and their cross, not one axis alone

all demographic/ethnicity purchase rates, absolute unit counts, national market sizes, competitor brand shares and retail prices are explicitly out of scope as authored facts here; they are either deferred to sibling KBs (kb2 consumer segmentation, kb3 trend/brand) or left as tagged [UNKNOWN] to be measured
exclusions: consumer demographic / age-cohort / gender / ethnicity / income segmentation and 'how many people buy' prevalence math (that is kb2_consumer_segmentation_method)
trend-signal reading, fad-vs-durable discrimination and the competitor brand + price-tier landscape map (that is kb3_trend_and_competitor_mapping)

the materials science of plating (rhodium/gold chemistry, thickness classes, nickel release, tarnish mechanism) and quality/cost value engineering (the jewel_materials specialist owns those; this KB uses only the FTC labeling definitions, not the process)

form/shape/style selection, sizing/fit systems and the launch set-of-six assortment decision (jewel_form and jewel_assortment specialists own those; this KB supplies the demand and finish read they consume)
COGS/landed-cost, pricing/margin and CAC/LTV unit economics (jewel_economics owns those; price bands appear here only as a finish/tier classification proxy, never as a cost or margin claim)
asserting any single national solid-vs-plated share percentage, category unit-sales count, or brand market share as a fact; this KB encodes how to estimate those, not the answers

competency_questions.question: What is the category taxonomy of fashion jewelry (earrings/necklaces/rings/bracelets/anklets) and its buyable subtypes, so demand can be read at the right granularity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CATEGORY_TAXONOMY names the five top categories and their principal subtypes (studs/hoops/drops/huggies/ear-cuffs; chains/pendants/chokers; bands/stackables/signets; bangles/cuffs/chain/tennis; anklets) as a [FACT] descriptive taxonomy and states that demand is read per subtype not per top category alone

competency_questions.question: What separates the fine tier from the fashion/costume tier, and why does the boundary matter for this venture?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINE_VS_FASHION_TIER defines fine (solid precious metal / natural stones, karat-marked, jeweler channel) versus fashion/costume (base-metal or plated, trend-driven, mass/DTC channel) and states the venture sits in fashion/costume

competency_questions.question: What are the FTC 16 CFR Part 23 definitions of gold-plated, gold electroplate, gold-filled/overlay, vermeil, rhodium and sterling silver, and what thresholds do they impose?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FTC_FINISH_DEFINITIONS states vermeil = sterling base with >=10k gold >=2.5um on significant surfaces, gold electroplate >= ~0.175um (heavy gold electroplate >=2.5um), gold-filled/overlay = mechanically bonded >=10k layer (gold-filled >=1/20 by weight), sterling = 92.5% silver, rhodium as a platinum-group plating, each tagged [FACT - 16 CFR 23] with thresholds flagged for verification

competency_questions.question: How do the finishes order into a material/value ladder from solid gold down to stainless/steel, and where does rhodium-plated silver sit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINISH_TAXONOMY orders solid gold > gold-filled > vermeil > gold-plated (base metal) > rhodium-plated sterling silver > stainless/steel/base with the durability-and-value rationale and places rhodium-over-silver as the bright-white tarnish-resistant fashion-tier finish

competency_questions.question: How is category demand sized from public data without a proprietary sales dataset, and how are the three proxies combined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BESTSELLER_RANK_METHOD, SEARCH_VOLUME_METHOD and ASSORTMENT_SHARE_METHOD each define a public-data proxy [METHOD] and DEMAND_TRIANGULATION combines them into a per-subtype demand ranking as an [ESTIMATE] with confidence, over a defined SAMPLE_FRAME_METHOD panel

competency_questions.question: What biases and lags does each demand proxy carry, and how are they kept from being over-read?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_BIAS_LEDGER enumerates rank-velocity vs absolute-volume, search-intent vs purchase, assortment-share vs sell-through, category-name conflation, seasonality and platform-audience skew, and states each proxy is directional not absolute

competency_questions.question: How can the solid-gold vs gold-plated share be estimated from public data without inventing a national percentage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOLID_VS_PLATED_ESTIMATE_METHOD classifies each sampled SKU by disclosed finish, weights by a demand proxy, computes an assortment-share and a demand-weighted share within a defined frame, and reports both as [ESTIMATE] with sampling caveats, explicitly refusing any single national unit-share fact

competency_questions.question: How is a finish claim on a listing verified against the FTC labeling rules so a mislabeled SKU is not miscounted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINISH_CLAIM_VERIFICATION checks disclosed base metal, karat of plate and micron/thickness against the 16 CFR 23 thresholds, flags vague terms (gold-tone, gold-color, gold-dipped) as non-FTC finish claims, and routes unverifiable claims to an [UNKNOWN] bucket rather than a finish class

competency_questions.question: How does retail price band act as a finish/tier proxy, and what are its limits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICE_BAND_PROXY uses observed listing price bands as a weak proxy for finish tier (fine >> gold-filled/vermeil > plated > steel), notes keystone-markup context [FACT-definition], and warns that perceived-value pricing breaks the proxy so it is corroborating not decisive

competency_questions.question: Why is fashion/costume (plated) the owner's tier rather than fine (solid) jewelry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FASHION_TIER_RATIONALE argues from the plating process fit, the ~18-25 price sensitivity and trend velocity, the base-metal/plated cost structure and the DTC channel, tying it to FINISH_TIER_SEGMENT_MAP, and marks the demand-share claims as [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD] not fact

competency_questions.question: What is the correct positioning of rhodium-plated silver in the fashion tier, and what is genuinely true about rhodium?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RHODIUM_POSITIONING states rhodium is a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant platinum-group metal commonly plated over sterling silver / white gold, corrects the owner's rough intuition precisely, and positions rhodium-over-silver as the premium white-metal option within fashion, tagged [FACT]

competency_questions.question: What does this KB deliberately leave [UNKNOWN] or hand off, and to whom, so no number is fabricated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNKNOWNS_LEDGER lists the un-authored quantities (absolute unit counts, exact national solid-vs-plated %, demographic/ethnicity rates, brand shares, prices) with their [UNKNOWN]/deferred tag and HANDOFF routes category+finish reads to kb2/kb3/jewel_assortment

competency_questions.question: How is the sampling frame defined so an assortment/best-seller read is representative rather than cherry-picked?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAMPLE_FRAME_METHOD defines the storefront/marketplace panel, the SKU inclusion rule, the time window and the survivorship/coverage caveats, so every downstream share is qualified by its frame

competency_questions.question: How do occasion, gifting and seasonality reshape category demand and require re-weighting the read over time?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONALITY_OCCASION names the gifting/holiday and occasion drivers, states that a point-in-time read must be seasonally qualified, and feeds a re-weighting back into the triangulation

glossary.definition: The precious tier: solid precious metal (10k-24k gold, platinum) and/or natural gemstones, karat/fineness-marked under FTC rules, sold through jewelers; durable and high unit value. Carried here only as the contrast pole to the fashion tier the venture targets.

The non-precious tier: base-metal or plated construction (brass, steel, zinc, plated silver), trend-driven, lower unit price, sold mass/DTC/social. The owner's tier; 'costume' and 'fashion' are used interchangeably for base-metal/plated pieces not marked as solid precious metal.

An electrolytically deposited gold (>=10k) coating on a base metal; FTC recognizes 'gold electroplate' at >= ~0.175 micron (about 7 millionths of an inch) and 'heavy gold electroplate' at >= 2.5 micron. Thinner deposits are 'gold flashed'/'gold washed'. [FACT - thresholds flagged for verification against current text]

A specific FTC finish: a base of sterling silver plated on all significant surfaces with gold (or gold alloy) of at least 10 karat and a minimum thickness of 2.5 microns; below that thickness or over a non-silver base it is not vermeil. [FACT]

A mechanically bonded (not electroplated) layer of at least 10k gold over a base metal; 'gold-filled' requires the gold layer be at least 1/20 (5%) of the item's total weight (for 10k+), with the karat disclosed; lighter bonds are 'gold overlay' / 'rolled gold plate (R.G.P.)'. More durable than electroplate. [FACT]
A silver alloy of at least 92.5% silver by weight (925 parts per 1000), the standard marked as 'sterling' or '925'; the balance is usually copper. [FACT]

An electroplated coating of rhodium, a hard, bright-white, highly reflective, tarnish- and corrosion-resistant platinum-group metal, commonly applied over sterling silver or white gold to give a bright white finish and slow tarnish; thin and eventually wears, requiring re-plating. [FACT - materials fact; process detail owned by jewel_materials]

The measure of gold purity by weight in 24ths: 24k = pure gold, 14k = 14/24 (~58.3%) gold; FTC requires the karat fineness of gold and of a gold plating to be disclosed. Distinct from 'carat', the gemstone weight unit. [FACT]

Using a marketplace's ordinal best-seller / popularity rank within a category node as a directional proxy for relative demand of a subtype; ordinal and velocity-driven, not an absolute unit count, and only comparable within the same category node and time window.

The share of listings (SKUs) a category or finish occupies within a defined storefront/marketplace frame; a supply-side proxy for demand that reflects what sellers stock, which lags and can diverge from actual sell-through, so it is read alongside demand-weighted proxies.

The proportion of solid precious-metal versus plated/base-metal pieces, computed within a defined sampled frame as either an assortment share (share of listings) or a demand-weighted share (weighted by a demand proxy); always an [ESTIMATE] qualified by its frame, never a national unit-sales fact.

The traditional retail convention of pricing at roughly 2x wholesale (a 50% gross margin); used here only to interpret why price bands separate finish tiers, not as a cost or margin claim about any specific product.

nodes.definition: Fix what this KB reasons about and the honesty discipline that binds every claim in it. Scope: two orthogonal cuts of the US fashion-jewelry catalog - category (earrings/necklaces/rings/bracelets/anklets) and finish tier (fine vs fashion; solid-gold vs gold-plated/vermeil/gold-filled vs rhodium-plated silver vs stainless/steel) - plus the public-data methods that size demand on each. Discipline: real, well-established domain facts (FTC 16 CFR Part 23 finish definitions; rhodium materials facts; sterling = 92.5% Ag; keystone-markup definition) are carried as [FACT] with basis; every demand quantity is either a [METHOD] to measure it or an [ESTIMATE] with method+confidence; anything not measurable here is an honest [UNKNOWN]. No market size, unit count, solid-vs-plated %, demographic/ethnicity rate, brand share or price is ever asserted as a measured fact in this KB.

included: the category and finish-tier dual scope
the [FACT]/[METHOD]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tagging contract
the no-fabricated-number rule
excluded: the substantive taxonomies and methods (later nodes)

pros.claim: Fixing the honesty contract first makes every later demand number auditable as method-or-estimate, not a guess
pros.example: a reader can trace any solid-vs-plated figure to its [ESTIMATE] tag and sampling frame rather than reading it as a national fact

cons.claim: A strict no-number rule frustrates a stakeholder who wants one headline percentage now
cons.example: the owner asking 'what percent is gold-plated' gets a method plus an estimate band, not a single number

failure_modes: letting a convenient round number slip in as fact without a method or estimate tag
scope-creeping into demographics, pricing or materials that sibling KBs own
acceptance_tests: the dual category/finish scope and the [FACT]/[METHOD]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tagging contract are stated with the explicit no-fabricated-number rule
revisit_triggers: the owner brief or build plan changes the KB's scope
a sibling KB boundary (kb2/kb3/materials/economics) is redrawn
a new public data source changes what is measurable vs [UNKNOWN]

base.update_signal: the scope or honesty contract is amended

nodes.definition: Establish the category spine at buyable granularity. Five top categories and their principal subtypes: EARRINGS (studs, hoops, huggies, drops/danglers, ear cuffs, threaders), NECKLACES (chains, pendants, chokers, lariats/Y-necklaces, layered sets), RINGS (bands, stackables, statement/cocktail, signets, adjustable), BRACELETS (bangles, cuffs, chain/link, tennis, beaded), and ANKLETS (chain, beaded, charm). Demand is not uniform across the tree: a top category can be flat while one subtype (e.g. huggie hoops, paperclip chains) drives it, so demand must be read per subtype and only then rolled up. This taxonomy is a [FACT] descriptive classification (industry-standard product types), not a demand claim; the demand weights on it come from the method nodes.

included: the five top categories and their principal subtypes
the read-per-subtype-then-roll-up rule
excluded: the demand weights on the tree (method nodes)

pros.claim: Reading demand per subtype prevents a hot subtype from being hidden inside a flat top-category average
pros.example: hoops surging while studs are flat is invisible at the 'earrings' level but decisive for assortment

cons.claim: Subtype granularity multiplies the sampling and classification work and can outrun the available signal
cons.example: some marketplaces do not expose a node fine enough to separate huggies from standard hoops

failure_modes: reading demand only at the five-category level and missing the driving subtype
inventing subtypes not grounded in how sellers/marketplaces actually categorize
acceptance_tests: the five categories and their principal subtypes are enumerated with the read-per-subtype-then-roll-up rule stated
revisit_triggers: a marketplace changes its category node structure
a new subtype emerges as a distinct buyable type
jewel_form republishes the construction taxonomy

base.update_signal: a marketplace taxonomy or a new subtype changes the tree

nodes.definition: Define the tier boundary the whole venture sits inside. FINE jewelry = solid precious metal (10k-24k gold, platinum) and/or natural gemstones, karat/fineness-marked under FTC rules, sold through jewelers, high unit value, durable, bought as investment/heirloom/milestone. FASHION / COSTUME jewelry = base-metal or plated construction (brass, steel, zinc, plated sterling), trend-driven, lower unit price, disposable-fashion cadence, sold mass-retail / DTC / social. The two are a spectrum, not a wall (demi-fine / vermeil / gold-filled bridge the middle), and the same category (a hoop, a chain) exists in both. The venture is a DTC plated line for ~18-25 buyers, so it sits in fashion/costume with a possible demi-fine (vermeil / rhodium-silver) reach; fine is carried only as the contrast pole. [FACT on the definitional boundary; the venture placement is an [ESTIMATE]-of-fit, not a market claim].

included: the fine-vs-fashion definitional boundary and the demi-fine bridge
the venture's placement in fashion/costume

pros.claim: A clear tier boundary keeps demand and finish reads from mixing an heirloom-buyer signal with a trend-buyer signal
pros.example: a solid-gold engagement-ring demand curve is irrelevant to a $25 plated-hoop line and is excluded up front

cons.claim: The demi-fine middle (vermeil, gold-filled, rhodium-silver) genuinely straddles the boundary, so a hard binary can mis-file bridge products
cons.example: a vermeil hoop is fashion in price cadence but fine-adjacent in construction and marketing

failure_modes: treating fine and fashion as one market and blending their demand signals
forcing a demi-fine bridge product cleanly into one tier and losing its dual nature
acceptance_tests: the fine-vs-fashion boundary, the demi-fine bridge, and the venture's placement in fashion/costume are stated with tags
revisit_triggers: the venture repositions toward demi-fine or fine
a demi-fine category blurs the boundary materially
the owner brief changes the target tier

base.update_signal: the venture tier placement or the tier boundary shifts

nodes.definition: Carry the controlling US finish definitions as [FACT], from the FTC Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries (16 CFR Part 23). VERMEIL: a sterling-silver base plated on all significant surfaces with >=10 karat gold at >= 2.5 micron thickness. GOLD ELECTROPLATE / GOLD-PLATED: an electrolytic >=10k gold coating at >= ~0.175 micron (~7 millionths inch); HEAVY GOLD ELECTROPLATE at >= 2.5 micron; thinner is 'gold flashed'/'gold washed'. GOLD-FILLED / GOLD OVERLAY / ROLLED GOLD PLATE: a mechanically bonded >=10k layer; 'gold-filled' requires the layer be >= 1/20 (5%) of total weight (for 10k+), lighter bonds are 'overlay'/'R.G.P.', karat disclosed. STERLING SILVER: >= 92.5% Ag (925). RHODIUM and other platinum-group platings are addressed under the platinum-group marking rules. KARAT fineness of gold and of any gold plate must be disclosed. Exact micron/karat thresholds are stated as [FACT - 16 CFR 23] but flagged for verification against the current published text before any labeling use.

included: the FTC definitions and thresholds for vermeil, gold electroplate, gold-filled/overlay, sterling, rhodium/PGM, karat disclosure
excluded: the demand or price implications (later nodes)

pros.claim: Anchoring on the FTC definitions gives every finish classification a citeable legal standard instead of loose marketing words
pros.example: a 'vermeil' listing can be tested against the >=10k / >=2.5um / sterling-base rule rather than taken at face value

cons.claim: The precise micron/karat thresholds must be verified against the live regulation text, so citing them from memory risks a stale figure
cons.example: a threshold restated slightly wrong would mislabel a borderline SKU

failure_modes: treating a marketing term (gold-tone, gold-dipped) as an FTC finish class
quoting a micron/karat threshold as exact without verifying the current 16 CFR 23 text
acceptance_tests: vermeil (>=10k, >=2.5um, sterling base), gold electroplate (>= ~0.175um; heavy >=2.5um), gold-filled (>=1/20 weight, mechanically bonded), sterling (>=92.5% Ag) and the karat-disclosure rule are stated as [FACT-16 CFR 23] with thresholds flagged for verification
revisit_triggers: the FTC amends the Jewelry Guides or a threshold
a labeling use requires the exact current text
a new finish term needs an FTC status ruling

base.update_signal: an FTC Jewelry Guides amendment or a threshold verification changes a definition

nodes.definition: Order the finishes into one durability-and-value ladder the demand read is segmented on, using the FTC definitions as the rungs: SOLID GOLD (10k-24k, fine) > GOLD-FILLED (mechanically bonded >=10k >=1/20 weight, most durable plated-family) > VERMEIL (>=10k >=2.5um over sterling) > GOLD ELECTROPLATE over base metal (heavy >=2.5um vs standard >= ~0.175um) > RHODIUM-PLATED STERLING SILVER (bright-white, tarnish-resistant PGM finish over 925) > STAINLESS/STEEL & bare base metal (brass/zinc, PVD or unplated). The ladder is orthogonal to the category tree: every category exists across every rung. Solid gold is the fine anchor; gold-filled/vermeil are the demi-fine bridge; electroplate, rhodium-silver and steel are the fashion core the venture lives in. Ordering by durability/value is a [FACT-backed] structuring; the demand weight on each rung is an [ESTIMATE] from the method nodes.

included: the solid>gold-filled>vermeil>electroplate>rhodium-silver>steel ladder
the orthogonality of finish and category
the fashion-core placement of electroplate/rhodium/steel
excluded: the rhodium materials science (RHODIUM_POSITIONING carries the fact; jewel_materials the process)

pros.claim: A single ordered finish ladder lets demand be segmented consistently and lets solid-vs-plated be computed on a defined scale
pros.example: classifying every sampled SKU onto one rung makes a plated-vs-solid share well-defined instead of ad hoc

cons.claim: A strict linear ladder compresses genuinely two-dimensional attributes (durability vs whiteness vs cost) into one order
cons.example: rhodium-silver is more tarnish-resistant than thin electroplate yet sits below vermeil on value - one axis cannot show both

failure_modes: conflating the finish ladder with the category tree instead of treating them as orthogonal
placing a bridge finish (vermeil, gold-filled) as if it were fashion-disposable or fine-solid rather than demi-fine
acceptance_tests: the ordered finish ladder from solid gold to steel is stated with each rung tied to its FTC definition and the finish/category orthogonality noted
revisit_triggers: an FTC definition change re-ranks a rung
a new finish (e.g. a durable PVD gold) enters the fashion core
the venture adds or drops a finish rung

base.update_signal: an FTC change or a new finish re-orders the ladder

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Define the frame every share and rank is read against, so results are representative rather than cherry-picked. Specify: the storefront/marketplace panel (which platforms and which category nodes - e.g. a broad marketplace fashion-jewelry node, one or more DTC storefronts, one aggregator), the SKU inclusion rule (in-stock, fashion-tier, US-shipping, within named category nodes), the time window (a stated date range, because ranks and assortments drift), and the coverage/survivorship caveats (sold-out and delisted SKUs vanish, sponsored placements distort, a single platform's audience is not the US market). Every downstream number is reported as 'within frame F', never as a national figure. Choosing and documenting the frame is the single biggest lever on whether an assortment or best-seller read is trustworthy.

included: the panel, SKU inclusion rule, time window and coverage caveats
the within-frame qualification on every result

pros.claim: A documented frame turns a share number into a reproducible, qualified estimate instead of a cherry-pick
pros.example: 'plated = X% of listings in frame F, Jun 2026' is checkable; 'plated is X% of the market' is not

cons.claim: A single accessible frame is never the US market, so even a clean within-frame number carries external-validity risk
cons.example: one marketplace over-indexes on ultra-cheap imports and understates demi-fine

failure_modes: reporting a share without naming its frame and letting it read as national
picking a frame that quietly excludes a tier (e.g. only ultra-budget listings) and biasing every downstream share
acceptance_tests: the panel, SKU inclusion rule, time window and coverage/survivorship caveats are specified and every result is qualified 'within frame F'
revisit_triggers: a platform is added to or dropped from the panel
a marketplace changes its category nodes or ranking exposure
the time window is refreshed for a new read

base.update_signal: the panel, category nodes or time window of the frame changes

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Use marketplace best-seller / popularity ranks within a category node as a directional demand proxy for subtypes. Procedure: within the frame, capture the ordinal best-seller rank (and, where exposed, review-count and review-velocity) of listings per subtype node, aggregate to a subtype-level rank signal, and compare subtypes only within the same node and window. Best-seller rank is ordinal and recency/velocity-weighted, so it signals what is selling fast now, not absolute lifetime volume, and cannot be differenced across categories with different node sizes. Review counts are a lagging cumulative proxy that biases toward older listings. Output is a per-subtype directional demand ranking [ESTIMATE, MED confidence], never a unit count.

included: ordinal best-seller rank and review-count/velocity as subtype demand proxies
within-node within-window comparability only

pros.claim: Best-seller rank is a near-real-time, publicly visible signal of what is actually selling, needing no proprietary data
pros.example: a subtype climbing the best-seller node week over week is a live demand uptick a static assortment read would miss

cons.claim: Rank is ordinal and velocity-driven, so it shows order not magnitude and can be gamed by promotions or sponsored slots
cons.example: a discounted SKU spikes in rank without a durable demand shift

failure_modes: reading an ordinal rank as an absolute or cross-category unit volume
trusting review counts as current demand when they are a cumulative lagging proxy
acceptance_tests: the ordinal best-seller-rank and review-count/velocity proxies are defined with the within-node within-window comparability limit and an [ESTIMATE] output tag
revisit_triggers: a marketplace changes how it exposes or computes best-seller rank
sponsored-placement contamination rises in the node
a fresh capture window is run

base.update_signal: a marketplace ranking mechanic or a new capture window changes the proxy

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Use keyword search volume and trend as a demand-intent proxy for categories/subtypes and finishes. Procedure: pull search-volume and relative-trend series (from a public keyword/trends tool) for a normalized query set covering each subtype ('gold hoop earrings', 'huggie earrings', 'paperclip necklace', 'rhodium plated silver ring') and each finish term, deduplicate synonyms, and read both level and slope. Search volume measures intent/interest upstream of purchase, leads best-seller rank in time, and captures off-marketplace demand, but conflates buyers with browsers/researchers, is distorted by brand and editorial spikes, and depends heavily on the chosen query set. Output is a per-subtype interest ranking [ESTIMATE, MED confidence], corroborating not replacing the purchase proxies.

included: search volume and trend slope as an intent proxy over a normalized query set
its lead-time and off-marketplace coverage strengths

pros.claim: Search volume captures upstream intent and off-marketplace demand that on-site ranks cannot see, and leads sales in time
pros.example: a rising 'rhodium plated ring' trend signals demand before it shows in any one store's best-seller list

cons.claim: Search intent is not purchase and is highly sensitive to the query set and to editorial/brand spikes
cons.example: a viral post inflates a term's volume without proportional buying

failure_modes: treating search interest as realized sales
letting a poorly chosen or synonym-collapsed query set bias the whole subtype ranking
acceptance_tests: the search-volume/trend intent proxy over a normalized query set is defined with its intent-not-purchase and query-set-sensitivity limits and an [ESTIMATE] output tag
revisit_triggers: the query set is revised or expanded
a viral/editorial spike distorts a term
the keyword tool's methodology changes

base.update_signal: the query set or the keyword-tool methodology changes

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Use retail assortment share - the share of listings a category, subtype or finish occupies within the frame - as a supply-side demand proxy. Procedure: enumerate SKUs in the frame, classify each by category/subtype and by finish rung, and compute share-of-SKUs per cut. Sellers stock to expected demand, so assortment share is an informative proxy, and it is the natural basis for the solid-vs-plated estimate because finish is a listing attribute. But it is supply-side: it reflects what sellers chose to stock (which lags demand and herds), over-weights easy-to-source cheap SKUs, and diverges from actual sell-through, so it must be read against the purchase proxies. Output is per-cut assortment shares [ESTIMATE], each qualified by frame.

included: share-of-listings by category/subtype and finish rung as a supply-side proxy
its role as the basis for the solid-vs-plated estimate
excluded: sell-through / demand-weighted share (needs a demand proxy)

pros.claim: Assortment share is directly countable from listings and is the natural axis for a finish-mix estimate
pros.example: share of SKUs marked vermeil vs electroplate vs steel in the frame is a computable finish-mix number

cons.claim: It is supply-side and herds, so a crowded category can reflect easy sourcing rather than strong demand
cons.example: cheap stud earrings flood a marketplace on low sourcing cost, overstating stud demand versus sell-through

failure_modes: reading share-of-listings as share-of-sales
classifying finish from marketing words rather than verified FTC-grade claims (see FINISH_CLAIM_VERIFICATION)
acceptance_tests: share-of-listings by category/subtype and by finish rung is defined as a supply-side proxy, qualified by frame, with the lag/herding limit and its role as the finish-mix basis stated
revisit_triggers: the frame or its category nodes change
a sourcing shift floods or empties a category
a fresh SKU enumeration is run

base.update_signal: the frame, a sourcing shift or a new enumeration changes the assortment shares

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Use observed listing price bands as a weak, corroborating proxy for finish tier. Within the frame, bucket SKUs by price and observe that finish tiers separate on price - fine solid gold >> gold-filled/vermeil > heavy electroplate > thin electroplate / rhodium-silver > bare steel/base - with the separation reflecting metal value and durability. Keystone markup (roughly 2x wholesale, ~50% gross margin) [FACT-definition] is the convention that makes retail price track underlying finish cost, which is why the proxy works at all. Its limits are severe: perceived-value and brand pricing routinely break the mapping (a branded plated piece can outprice an unbranded vermeil one), promotions distort bands, and price says nothing about category. So price band is corroborating evidence for a finish classification, never decisive, and is never used here as a cost or margin claim (jewel_economics owns those).

included: price bands as a weak corroborating finish-tier proxy
the keystone-markup rationale for why it works
the perceived-value/brand limits
excluded: using price as a category-demand signal

pros.claim: Price bands cheaply corroborate a finish classification and flag suspicious listings where price and claimed finish disagree
pros.example: a $9 'vermeil' listing whose price sits in the bare-steel band is a red flag for a mislabeled finish

cons.claim: Perceived-value and brand pricing break the price-to-finish mapping, so the proxy is only ever corroborating
cons.example: a hyped DTC brand's plated hoop priced above an unbranded vermeil hoop inverts the expected order

failure_modes: treating price band as a decisive finish classifier instead of corroborating evidence
letting a price observation leak into a cost or margin claim this KB does not own
acceptance_tests: price bands are defined as a weak corroborating finish-tier proxy with the keystone-markup rationale and the perceived-value/brand limits, explicitly not a cost/margin claim
revisit_triggers: a promotional cycle distorts price bands in the frame
a brand-pricing shift breaks the tier separation
jewel_economics revises the pricing context

base.update_signal: a promotion cycle or a brand-pricing shift changes the price-tier mapping

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Combine the three proxies - best-seller rank (purchase, near-real-time), search volume (intent, leading), assortment share (supply-side, structural) - into one per-subtype demand ranking, because no single proxy is trustworthy alone. Procedure: normalize each proxy to a within-frame rank or z-score per subtype, weight by reliability for the decision at hand (rank highest for what-sells-now, search for what-is-emerging, assortment for what-is-crowded), and combine into a composite ordinal ranking with an explicit agreement flag: subtypes where all three agree are high-confidence, split signals are low-confidence and flagged for a poll (jewel_poll). The output is a ranked, confidence-tagged category/subtype demand list [ESTIMATE], never a unit forecast. Triangulation converts three biased directional signals into one honest ranking with stated confidence.

included: normalizing, weighting and combining the three proxies into a confidence-tagged ordinal ranking
the agree/split confidence flag

pros.claim: Triangulating three independent-biased proxies is far more robust than any one and exposes disagreement honestly
pros.example: a subtype ranked high on all three is a confident bet; one high only on search is flagged as unproven interest

cons.claim: The weighting is a judgment call, so a composite can encode the analyst's prior if the weights are not stated
cons.example: over-weighting assortment share tilts the ranking toward crowded cheap categories

failure_modes: hiding the weighting scheme so the composite looks objective
collapsing a split-signal subtype into a false-confident rank instead of flagging it for a poll
acceptance_tests: the three proxies are normalized, explicitly weighted and combined into a confidence-tagged ordinal ranking with an agree/split flag and an [ESTIMATE] tag
revisit_triggers: a proxy is added, dropped or re-weighted
a poll result updates a split-signal subtype
a fresh capture changes the composite

base.update_signal: a proxy weighting, a new capture or a poll result changes the composite ranking

nodes.definition: Maintain the explicit ledger of each proxy's bias and lag so the triangulated ranking is read as directional, not absolute. Best-seller rank: ordinal (order not magnitude), velocity/recency-weighted, gameable by promotion/sponsored slots, incomparable across nodes. Search volume: intent not purchase, query-set-dependent, spiked by editorial/viral events, conflates researchers with buyers. Assortment share: supply-side, herds, lags demand, over-weights cheap easy-to-source SKUs, diverges from sell-through. Cross-cutting: seasonality (a point-in-time read is a snapshot), platform-audience skew (one marketplace is not the US buyer), category-name conflation (a 'necklace' node mixing chains and pendants), and survivorship (sold-out/delisted winners vanish). The ledger's rule: report every demand statement with its dominant bias attached and never promote a ranking to an absolute share or count.

included: the per-proxy and cross-cutting biases/lags
the report-with-bias, never-promote-to-absolute rule

pros.claim: A standing bias ledger stops a directional ranking from being over-read as a market share or a unit count
pros.example: flagging assortment share as supply-side herding prevents 'most-listed' being reported as 'most-bought'

cons.claim: Heavy caveating can make the read feel unusable to a decision-maker who wants a clean answer
cons.example: a stakeholder may push for a single ranked list without the confidence flags

failure_modes: dropping the bias tag when a ranking is summarized upward
correcting for one bias (e.g. seasonality) while silently ignoring another (survivorship)
acceptance_tests: the per-proxy biases (rank, search, assortment) and cross-cutting biases (seasonality, platform skew, name conflation, survivorship) are enumerated with the never-promote-to-absolute rule
revisit_triggers: a new proxy or data source adds a bias
a seasonal boundary is crossed
a platform-audience shift changes the skew

base.update_signal: a new proxy, season or platform shift changes the bias ledger

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Verify a listing's finish claim against the FTC 16 CFR 23 thresholds before it is counted into a finish class, so a mislabeled or vague SKU does not corrupt the solid-vs-plated estimate. Check the disclosed base metal (sterling vs brass/steel), the karat of the plate, and the stated thickness/micron against the definitions: 'vermeil' requires sterling base + >=10k + >=2.5um; 'gold-filled' requires a mechanically bonded >=10k >=1/20-weight layer; 'gold electroplate' requires >= ~0.175um. Treat vague marketing terms - 'gold-tone', 'gold-color', 'gold-dipped', '18k gold plated' with no thickness, 'waterproof gold' - as NON-verified finish claims. Route each SKU to: a verified finish rung (claim meets the definition), a demoted rung (claim implies less than it says), or an [UNKNOWN] bucket (unverifiable). This keeps the finish-mix estimate honest at the SKU level.

included: checking base metal, karat and thickness against FTC thresholds
the verified/demoted/[UNKNOWN] routing of each SKU's finish claim
excluded: physically testing a product (materials lab, jewel_materials)

pros.claim: Verifying claims against FTC thresholds stops mislabeled and vague listings from inflating a finish class
pros.example: '18k gold plated' with no micron is routed to [UNKNOWN] rather than counted as heavy electroplate

cons.claim: Most listings under-disclose thickness, so a large [UNKNOWN] bucket can dominate and widen the estimate
cons.example: if 40% of SKUs give no micron, the plated-mix band is correspondingly wide

failure_modes: counting a marketing term (gold-tone, gold-dipped) as an FTC finish class
assigning a finish rung to a claim that omits the base metal or thickness needed to verify it
acceptance_tests: base metal, karat and thickness are checked against the FTC thresholds and each SKU is routed to a verified rung, a demoted rung, or an [UNKNOWN] bucket, with vague terms treated as non-verified
revisit_triggers: an FTC threshold is amended
platform disclosure norms change what listings reveal
a spot re-audit of the [UNKNOWN] bucket is run

base.update_signal: an FTC threshold or platform disclosure norm changes verification

nodes.definition: [METHOD] Estimate the solid-gold vs gold-plated (and broader finish-mix) share without inventing a national percentage. Procedure: over the defined frame, take each SKU's FINISH_CLAIM_VERIFICATION result, then compute two distinct shares: (1) ASSORTMENT share = share of listings on each finish rung, and (2) DEMAND-WEIGHTED share = the same weighting each SKU by a demand proxy (best-seller rank / review velocity), which better approximates share-of-sales. Report both, plus the [UNKNOWN]-bucket size, as an [ESTIMATE] band with confidence, always qualified 'within frame F, date D'. Explicitly refuse to state a single national solid-vs-plated unit-share percentage - that requires point-of-sale data this KB does not have. The honest answer to the owner's 'what percent is gold-plated' is a method plus a frame-qualified estimate band with its uncertainty, never one number.

included: assortment share and demand-weighted share of each finish rung within a frame
the [UNKNOWN]-bucket reporting and the refusal of a national point figure
excluded: the demographic split of who buys which finish (kb2)

pros.claim: Reporting both an assortment and a demand-weighted share with its frame gives an honest, reproducible finish-mix without a fabricated national figure
pros.example: 'within frame F, plated ~ a majority of listings and a larger majority demand-weighted, [UNKNOWN] ~15%' is defensible where a single national % is not

cons.claim: Two frame-qualified bands plus an [UNKNOWN] bucket are harder to act on than one headline number the owner asked for
cons.example: a decision-maker wanting '70% plated' must accept a band and a caveat instead

failure_modes: collapsing the estimate into a single national percentage the data cannot support
reporting only assortment share (supply-side) as if it were share-of-sales
acceptance_tests: both assortment and demand-weighted finish-rung shares are computed within a named frame with the [UNKNOWN]-bucket size and an [ESTIMATE] band, and any single national unit-share figure is explicitly refused
revisit_triggers: a new frame or capture window is run
point-of-sale or panel data becomes available to tighten the estimate
the [UNKNOWN] bucket is re-audited

base.update_signal: a new frame, POS data or an [UNKNOWN]-bucket re-audit changes the finish-mix estimate

nodes.definition: Compose the KB's category-demand output: a ranked, confidence-tagged list of categories and subtypes by estimated US fashion-jewelry demand, drawn from the triangulated composite and qualified by the bias ledger. State it as tiers (high-confidence / medium / flagged-for-poll) rather than false-precise ordinals, attach each subtype's dominant supporting proxy and its dominant bias, and mark the whole as [ESTIMATE, within frame F, date D]. This is the demand read the assortment specialist consumes to shortlist categories and the poll specialist uses to choose what to test. It deliberately stops short of unit forecasts, brand attribution and demographic splits, which are [UNKNOWN] here or owned by sibling KBs.

included: the tiered, confidence-tagged category/subtype demand ranking as [ESTIMATE]
each subtype's supporting proxy and dominant bias
excluded: unit forecasts, brand attribution, demographic splits (out of scope / sibling KBs)

pros.claim: A tiered confidence-tagged ranking is directly usable by the assortment and poll specialists without overstating precision
pros.example: handing 'high-confidence: hoops, layered necklaces; test: anklets' lets the poll target the uncertain subtypes

cons.claim: Tiers hide within-tier order, so a decision needing a strict top-6 must still commit beyond what the data resolves
cons.example: six subtypes in the high tier cannot all be ranked 1-6 from proxies alone

failure_modes: presenting the ranking as precise ordinals the proxies cannot support
dropping the frame/date qualifier when the ranking is passed downstream
acceptance_tests: a tiered, confidence-tagged category/subtype demand ranking is produced as [ESTIMATE] with each subtype's supporting proxy and dominant bias and a frame/date qualifier
revisit_triggers: a fresh capture updates the composite
a poll resolves a flagged subtype
the assortment specialist requests a re-cut at a different granularity

base.update_signal: a new capture, poll result or re-cut request changes the ranking

nodes.definition: Build the cross-map that is the KB's second output: category/subtype on one axis, finish rung on the other, populated with the finish-mix estimates so the venture can see where fashion-tier demand concentrates. For each high-demand subtype, show its estimated finish mix (e.g. hoops skew electroplate + steel; chains span vermeil to steel; statement rings skew plated) as [ESTIMATE] within frame, with the solid tier marked as the fine contrast pole. The map exposes the addressable fashion/plated cells (where the venture can compete on plated construction) versus the fine cells it does not serve, and flags demi-fine (vermeil / rhodium-silver) cells as the optional premium reach. It is the joint category-and-finish read the assortment and pricing specialists need, kept as estimate-plus-frame, never asserted as market fact.

included: the category-by-finish cross-map populated with frame-qualified finish-mix estimates
the addressable fashion/plated cells vs fine cells vs demi-fine reach
excluded: the go-decision on which cells to launch (jewel_assortment)

pros.claim: Crossing category with finish shows where plated demand actually concentrates, which neither axis alone reveals
pros.example: the map showing hoops-in-electroplate as a dense addressable cell directs the venture better than 'earrings sell' plus 'plated sells' separately

cons.claim: Each cell's finish mix inherits the widest of its inputs' uncertainty, so sparse cells are soft
cons.example: an anklet-x-vermeil cell may have too few sampled SKUs to estimate reliably

failure_modes: reading a sparse cell's estimate as firm despite thin sampling
collapsing the two-axis map back to a one-axis story and losing the addressable-cell insight
acceptance_tests: the category-by-finish cross-map is populated with frame-qualified finish-mix [ESTIMATE]s, marking addressable fashion/plated cells, the fine contrast pole and the demi-fine reach
revisit_triggers: a finish-mix or demand estimate updates a cell
a sparse cell gets more sampled SKUs
the venture changes which finish rungs it offers

base.update_signal: a cell's finish-mix or demand estimate, or the offered finish set, changes the map

nodes.definition: State the genuine facts about rhodium and position rhodium-plated silver within the fashion tier, sharpening the owner's rough intuition. [FACT] Rhodium is a platinum-group metal: hard, extremely reflective, bright white, and highly resistant to tarnish and corrosion. It is electroplated in a thin layer, commonly over sterling silver or white gold, to give a bright white finish and to slow the tarnish that sterling silver (which reacts with sulfur in air) would otherwise show; the owner's 'makes silver shiny and keeps it from un-shining' is essentially correct, made precise here. The plating is thin and wears with use, so it eventually needs re-plating - a durability caveat, not a permanent coat. In the finish ladder, rhodium-over-sterling is the premium white-metal fashion option: brighter and more tarnish-resistant than bare or thinly-plated silver, distinct from the yellow gold-plated family, and a natural demi-fine reach for the venture. The plating chemistry and thickness engineering belong to jewel_materials; this node carries only the demand-relevant materials fact and its market positioning.

included: the rhodium materials facts (PGM, hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant, plated over silver/white gold, wears)
rhodium-over-silver as the premium white-metal fashion position

pros.claim: Getting the rhodium facts precisely right corrects the owner's intuition and grounds a credible white-metal positioning
pros.example: stating rhodium is a tarnish-resistant PGM that wears and needs re-plating both validates and sharpens the owner's understanding

cons.claim: The 'needs re-plating' durability caveat complicates a simple 'stays shiny forever' marketing line
cons.example: a claim of permanent shine would misstate the wear behavior and risk an FTC-style overclaim

failure_modes: overclaiming rhodium as a permanent tarnish-proof coat rather than a thin wearing layer
straying into plating-process detail that jewel_materials owns
acceptance_tests: rhodium is stated as a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant platinum-group metal plated over sterling silver/white gold that wears and needs re-plating, positioned as the premium white-metal fashion finish, tagged [FACT]
revisit_triggers: jewel_materials revises the rhodium/thickness facts
a new white-metal finish competes with rhodium-silver
the venture adds or drops rhodium-silver from its range

base.update_signal: a rhodium materials-fact revision or a range change updates the positioning

nodes.definition: Capture how occasion, gifting and seasonality reshape category demand so a point-in-time read is not mistaken for a steady state. Fashion-jewelry demand pulses with gifting peaks (winter holidays, Valentine's, Mother's Day, graduation, wedding season) and with occasion contexts (everyday/self-purchase, going-out, bridal/bridesmaid, workwear), and different categories index differently - e.g. pendants and bracelets over-index as gifts, everyday studs and hoops are steadier self-purchase. A best-seller or search read taken in one week is a seasonal snapshot; to be usable it must be seasonally qualified and, where possible, read as a trailing window or year-over-year to separate a durable subtype from a holiday spike. This node feeds a re-weighting back into the triangulation and flags which subtype rankings are seasonally sensitive. Occasion/gifting mix is a [METHOD]-plus-[FACT-pattern] read; specific gift-vs-self purchase rates are [UNKNOWN] here and belong to kb2.

included: gifting/holiday peaks and occasion contexts reshaping category demand
the seasonal-qualification and trailing-window rule
the re-weighting feedback into triangulation

pros.claim: Seasonally qualifying the read prevents a holiday spike from being mistaken for durable demand
pros.example: a pendant subtype topping ranks in December is flagged as a gifting peak, not a year-round winner

cons.claim: Separating durable demand from seasonal spikes needs a time series a single snapshot lacks
cons.example: without a trailing window, a one-week capture cannot tell steady hoops from a seasonal surge

failure_modes: reading a single-week snapshot as steady-state demand
attributing a gifting-driven spike to durable self-purchase demand
acceptance_tests: the gifting/holiday and occasion drivers, the seasonal-qualification/trailing-window rule and the re-weighting feedback into triangulation are stated with gift-vs-self rates left [UNKNOWN] to kb2
revisit_triggers: a seasonal boundary (holiday, Valentine's, wedding season) is crossed
a trailing-window capture becomes available
kb2 supplies occasion/gifting rates

base.update_signal: a seasonal boundary, a trailing-window capture or kb2 occasion data changes the read

nodes.definition: Argue, from the category and finish reads, why fashion/costume (plated) is the owner's tier rather than fine (solid). The case rests on structural fit, not a market-size claim: (1) the venture's core capability is plating (the supply-side vertical builds electroplating / PVD), so the product is definitionally plated/base-metal, i.e. fashion tier; (2) the target buyer (~18-25 women per the owner brief) is price-sensitive and trend-driven, matching fashion's lower price points and faster refresh cadence rather than fine jewelry's high-ticket milestone purchases; (3) the finish ladder places electroplate, rhodium-silver and steel in the fashion core where base-metal + plating cost structure supports accessible pricing; (4) DTC / social selling and the planned Instagram/TikTok poll fit fashion's trend-velocity, impulse-purchase behavior. Demi-fine (vermeil / rhodium-silver) is the optional premium reach. All demand-share support is [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]; the tier choice is a structural-fit argument, and the fine tier is excluded as a target, retained only as contrast.

included: the structural-fit argument for fashion/costume (plating capability, ~18-25 buyer, cost structure, DTC/social)
demi-fine as optional reach, fine as excluded contrast
excluded: the demographic sizing of the ~18-25 buyer (kb2)

pros.claim: Grounding the tier choice in capability and buyer fit makes it robust to the market numbers this KB cannot assert
pros.example: the venture builds plating rigs, so a plated/fashion product is the fit regardless of any national share figure

cons.claim: A structural-fit argument does not prove the fashion tier is the most profitable or least competitive route
cons.example: fashion/costume is also the most crowded, low-margin tier - fit does not equal easy

failure_modes: dressing the tier choice in fabricated market-share numbers instead of the structural-fit argument
ignoring that the fashion tier's crowding/margin pressure is the cost of the fit
acceptance_tests: the fashion/costume tier is justified by plating capability, the ~18-25 trend/price-sensitive buyer, the plated cost structure and DTC/social fit, with demi-fine as reach and fine excluded, all demand support tagged [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]
revisit_triggers: the venture's capability or target buyer changes
a demi-fine or fine pivot is considered
kb2/economics change the buyer or margin picture

base.update_signal: a capability, buyer or tier-strategy change updates the rationale

nodes.definition: Enumerate, honestly, everything this KB deliberately does NOT answer as a fact, so no downstream reader mistakes an absence for a gap in the method. Hard [UNKNOWN]s here: absolute category unit-sales counts and national market size (no POS data); a single national solid-vs-plated unit-share percentage (only frame-qualified [ESTIMATE] bands are produced); which ethnicity / demographic buys what and at what rate (deferred to kb2, and only ever as a research method with ethics caveats, never invented rates); which brands buyers actually buy and their shares (deferred to kb3); actual retail prices and margins (owned by jewel_economics; price appears here only as a finish proxy). What IS delivered: the category taxonomy and finish ladder [FACT], the demand-sizing and finish-mix [METHOD]s, and the frame-qualified [ESTIMATE] rankings and maps. The ledger's discipline: any question of the form 'how many / what % / which ethnicity / which brand / what price' is answered with a method or a deferral, never a guess.

included: the explicit [UNKNOWN]/deferred list (unit counts, national %, demographics, brands, prices)
the method-or-deferral-never-a-guess discipline

pros.claim: An explicit unknowns ledger makes the KB's honesty auditable and pre-empts pressure to fabricate the missing numbers
pros.example: the owner's 'which ethnicity buys' is logged as a kb2 method-with-ethics deferral, not answered with an invented rate

cons.claim: A long unknowns list can read as the KB under-delivering to a stakeholder expecting hard numbers
cons.example: a reader wanting a market size sees it listed as [UNKNOWN] rather than estimated

failure_modes: letting a deferred or [UNKNOWN] quantity be filled with a convenient guess downstream
conflating a method-deferral (measurable elsewhere) with a true [UNKNOWN] (not measurable)
acceptance_tests: the unit-count, national-%, demographic, brand and price quantities are listed as [UNKNOWN]/deferred with the method-or-deferral-never-a-guess rule, and the delivered [FACT]/[METHOD]/[ESTIMATE] items are named
revisit_triggers: a sibling KB or a data source makes a deferred quantity measurable
the owner presses for a fabricated number
a new [UNKNOWN] is discovered in the read

base.update_signal: a deferred quantity becomes measurable or a new [UNKNOWN] is found

nodes.definition: Compose the segment's hand-off and stop cleanly at the boundary. Deliver: (1) the FACT taxonomies - category tree and FTC-anchored finish ladder; (2) the METHODs - the frame definition, the three demand proxies and their triangulation, finish-claim verification and the solid-vs-plated estimate; (3) the ESTIMATE outputs - the tiered category/subtype demand ranking, the category-by-finish segment map, and the fashion-tier rationale with rhodium positioning; (4) the UNKNOWNS ledger. Route them: the category demand ranking and segment map feed jewel_assortment (which subtypes/finishes to shortlist for the launch six) and jewel_poll (which categories to test); the finish ladder and rhodium/FTC facts feed jewel_materials and jewel_economics as the market-facing finish definitions; the demographic, brand and price [UNKNOWN]s route to kb2, kb3 and jewel_economics respectively. Every number handed off keeps its [FACT]/[METHOD]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tag and its frame; nothing is promoted to an unqualified market fact at the boundary.

included: the packaged FACT/METHOD/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN deliverables and their routing to sibling KBs and specialists
the keep-the-tag, keep-the-frame boundary discipline
excluded: the poll instrument, demographic sizing, brand map and pricing (jewel_poll/kb2/kb3/economics)

pros.claim: A tagged, routed hand-off lets each downstream specialist consume exactly the category/finish read it needs without inheriting a fabricated number
pros.example: jewel_assortment gets a confidence-tiered subtype ranking plus the addressable finish cells, not a false national share

cons.claim: Handing off bands and tags rather than point answers pushes the resolving work (polls, POS data) downstream
cons.example: the assortment specialist must still run a poll to break ties the proxies could not resolve

failure_modes: stripping the [ESTIMATE]/frame qualifiers when packaging the hand-off
overstepping into the assortment, poll, demographic or pricing work the hand-off only feeds
acceptance_tests: the FACT taxonomies, METHODs, ESTIMATE outputs and UNKNOWNS ledger are packaged and routed to the named sibling KBs/specialists with every item keeping its tag and frame and no promotion to unqualified fact
revisit_triggers: a downstream specialist requests a different cut or granularity
a sibling KB resolves a deferred [UNKNOWN]
a fresh capture updates the estimates handed off

base.update_signal: a downstream request or a resolved [UNKNOWN] changes the hand-off

conflict_axes.name: supply_side_vs_demand_side_signal
conflict_axes.description: Assortment share reflects what sellers stock (supply-side, herds, lags) while best-seller rank reflects what buyers buy (demand-side); a crowded category can be slow-selling and a scarce one hot.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight the purchase proxy higher for what-sells decisions and treat a large assortment/rank divergence as a herding artifact to poll-test

conflict_axes.name: search_intent_vs_realized_purchase
conflict_axes.description: Search volume is upstream intent that leads sales; best-seller rank is realized purchase; the two diverge in time and can mislead if blended.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry search as a leading indicator and require purchase confirmation before acting; report the lead/lag rather than one blended figure

conflict_axes.name: single_headline_number_vs_honest_band
conflict_axes.description: The owner wants one figure ('what % is gold-plated', 'which sells most') while the public data supports only frame-qualified estimate bands and tiers.

conflict_axes.name: category_axis_vs_finish_axis
conflict_axes.description: Demand can be read by category (what type) or by finish (what material/tier); either axis alone hides where addressable plated demand actually concentrates.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read both axes and their cross (the segment map); a decision needs the category-by-finish cell, not one axis

conflict_axes.name: fashion_fit_vs_fashion_crowding
conflict_axes.description: The fashion/costume tier fits the venture's plating capability and young-buyer target, but it is also the most crowded, lowest-margin tier.
poles: commit to fashion on capability fit
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose fashion on structural fit while carrying the crowding/margin cost forward to jewel_economics and a demi-fine reach as differentiation

conflict_axes.name: marketing_finish_words_vs_ftc_definitions
conflict_axes.description: Listings use loose finish words ('gold-tone', '18k plated', 'gold-dipped') while the FTC defines strict thresholds; counting the words inflates finish classes.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verify each claim against 16 CFR 23 thresholds and route unverifiable ones to [UNKNOWN] rather than a finish rung

conflict_axes.name: price_as_finish_proxy_vs_perceived_value
conflict_axes.description: Price bands track finish cost via keystone markup, but perceived-value and brand pricing break the mapping, so price is only weak corroboration.
poles: distrust price as a finish signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use price only to corroborate or flag a finish classification, never to decide it; a branded plated piece can outprice a vermeil one

conflict_axes.name: point_in_time_snapshot_vs_durable_demand
conflict_axes.description: A single-week best-seller/search capture is a seasonal snapshot; durable demand needs a trailing window, and gifting spikes masquerade as steady demand.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: seasonally qualify every snapshot and prefer trailing/year-over-year windows to separate durable subtypes from holiday spikes

conflict_axes.name: top_category_rollup_vs_subtype_granularity
conflict_axes.description: Reading demand at the five-category level is simpler but hides a hot subtype inside a flat category; subtype granularity is richer but can outrun the signal.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read at subtype granularity where the frame exposes it and roll up only after, flagging subtypes the frame cannot separate

edge_cases.description: A listing says '18k gold plated' with no stated micron/thickness, so it cannot be verified as gold electroplate vs heavy electroplate
edge_cases.trigger: a finish claim omits the base metal or thickness needed to test it against 16 CFR 23
edge_cases.mitigation: route the SKU to the [UNKNOWN] finish bucket and report its size; do not assign it a finish rung

edge_cases.description: A 'vermeil' listing priced in the bare-steel band signals a mislabeled or non-compliant finish claim
edge_cases.trigger: a finish claim and the price band disagree sharply
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the SKU for finish re-verification and, if unresolved, demote it or route to [UNKNOWN] rather than counting it as vermeil

edge_cases.description: A subtype tops best-seller rank on a deep promotion while its search and assortment signals are flat, faking a demand surge
edge_cases.trigger: a promotion or sponsored placement spikes rank without durable demand
edge_cases.mitigation: cross-check the rank spike against search/assortment and a trailing window; treat a lone rank spike as promotional until corroborated

edge_cases.description: The owner asks for a single national 'percent gold-plated' figure and pushes to drop the caveats
edge_cases.trigger: pressure to convert a frame-qualified band into one headline percentage
edge_cases.mitigation: deliver the assortment and demand-weighted share bands with their frame and [UNKNOWN] bucket and explain why a national point figure needs POS data not held here

edge_cases.description: The chosen marketplace over-indexes on ultra-cheap imports, so the frame understates demi-fine (vermeil/gold-filled) demand
edge_cases.trigger: a single-platform frame with a skewed audience is treated as the US market
edge_cases.mitigation: widen the panel across platforms and qualify every share as within-frame; never generalize one platform to the US buyer

edge_cases.description: A marketplace 'necklaces' node mixes chains, pendants and chokers, conflating distinct subtypes
edge_cases.trigger: a category node is coarser than the subtype taxonomy
edge_cases.mitigation: re-split the node by title/attribute parsing where possible, else report at the coarser node and flag the conflation

edge_cases.description: A one-week December capture ranks pendants top, which is a gifting spike not durable demand
edge_cases.trigger: a point-in-time read is taken inside a gifting peak
edge_cases.mitigation: seasonally qualify the read and use a trailing/year-over-year window before calling a subtype durable

edge_cases.description: Rhodium-plated silver is marketed as permanently tarnish-proof, overstating a thin wearing plating
edge_cases.trigger: a durability claim ignores that rhodium plating wears and needs re-plating
edge_cases.mitigation: state rhodium as tarnish-resistant but a thin wearing layer needing re-plating; avoid a permanent-shine overclaim

edge_cases.description: A sold-out or delisted winning SKU vanishes from the frame, biasing the read toward slower survivors (survivorship)
edge_cases.trigger: the capture only sees currently-listed, in-stock SKUs
edge_cases.mitigation: note survivorship in the frame caveats and, where possible, capture sold-out/best-seller history to recover winners

edge_cases.description: The [UNKNOWN] finish bucket grows so large (many listings omit thickness) that the solid-vs-plated band is too wide to act on
edge_cases.trigger: widespread under-disclosure of plate thickness in the frame
edge_cases.mitigation: report the [UNKNOWN] share explicitly, tighten via a sampled deep-dive on a subset, and route the residual to a poll or supplier query

edge_cases.description: A demand-share estimate is quoted downstream without its frame/date qualifier and reads as a national market fact
edge_cases.trigger: the [ESTIMATE]/frame tag is stripped when the read is summarized upward
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the tag and frame attached at every hand-off and refuse promotion to an unqualified fact

edge_cases.description: A sparse segment-map cell (e.g. anklet-x-vermeil) has too few sampled SKUs to estimate its finish mix reliably
edge_cases.trigger: a category-by-finish cell falls below a minimum sample size
edge_cases.mitigation: mark the cell low-confidence or [UNKNOWN] rather than reporting a point, and gather more SKUs before relying on it

workflow.action: Fix scope and the honesty tagging contract
workflow.description: State the dual category/finish scope and the [FACT]/[METHOD]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] discipline with the no-fabricated-number rule
workflow.gate: the dual scope and tagging contract are stated with the no-fabricated-number rule

workflow.description: Enumerate the five categories and their principal subtypes at buyable granularity
workflow.gate: the five categories and their subtypes are enumerated with the read-per-subtype rule

workflow.action: Carry the FTC finish definitions and build the finish ladder
workflow.description: State the 16 CFR 23 definitions as [FACT] and order the finishes into the solid-to-steel ladder, orthogonal to category
workflow.gate: the FTC definitions and the ordered finish ladder are stated with finish/category orthogonality

workflow.description: Specify the panel, SKU inclusion rule, time window and coverage caveats so every read is within-frame
workflow.gate: the panel, inclusion rule, window and caveats are specified and results are qualified within-frame

workflow.description: Compute best-seller-rank, search-volume and assortment-share proxies per subtype/finish within the frame
workflow.gate: each proxy is computed with its comparability limit and an [ESTIMATE] tag

workflow.description: Normalize, explicitly weight and combine the three proxies into a confidence-tagged ordinal ranking with an agree/split flag
workflow.gate: the weighted composite with agree/split confidence flags is produced as [ESTIMATE]

workflow.description: Enumerate each proxy's bias/lag and the cross-cutting biases and bind the never-promote-to-absolute rule
workflow.gate: the per-proxy and cross-cutting biases are enumerated with the never-promote rule

workflow.action: Verify finish claims and estimate solid-vs-plated share
workflow.description: Verify each SKU's finish against FTC thresholds, then compute assortment and demand-weighted finish-rung shares with the [UNKNOWN] bucket
workflow.gate: both shares are computed within a frame with the [UNKNOWN] bucket and a national point figure refused

workflow.description: Cross category with finish, populate cells with frame-qualified finish-mix estimates, mark addressable plated cells
workflow.gate: the cross-map is populated with frame-qualified estimates marking addressable, fine and demi-fine cells

workflow.description: Apply the occasion/seasonality read as a re-weighting and state the rhodium-over-silver facts and positioning
workflow.gate: the seasonal qualification/re-weighting and the rhodium [FACT] positioning are stated

workflow.action: State the fashion-tier rationale and the demand ranking
workflow.description: Produce the tiered category demand ranking and the structural-fit argument for the fashion/costume tier
workflow.gate: the tiered ranking and the fashion-tier structural-fit argument are stated with [ESTIMATE]/[METHOD] tags

workflow.action: Log unknowns and compose the hand-off
workflow.description: Enumerate the [UNKNOWN]s/deferrals and package the FACT/METHOD/ESTIMATE deliverables routed to sibling KBs and specialists
workflow.gate: the unknowns are logged and the tagged, frame-qualified deliverables are routed with no promotion to fact

dominance_rules.rule: The FTC 16 CFR 23 definition dominates any listing's marketing finish word
dominance_rules.rationale: loose terms like 'gold-tone', '18k plated (no micron)' or 'gold-dipped' are not FTC finish classes
dominance_rules.trigger: a listing's finish word is used to classify a SKU
dominance_rules.action: verify against the FTC thresholds and route unverifiable claims to [UNKNOWN], never counting the marketing word as a finish rung

dominance_rules.rule: The purchase proxy dominates the supply-side proxy for a what-sells decision
dominance_rules.rationale: assortment share reflects seller herding and lags demand, while best-seller rank reflects actual buying
dominance_rules.trigger: assortment share and best-seller rank disagree on a subtype
dominance_rules.action: weight best-seller rank higher and flag the divergence as a herding/sourcing artifact to poll-test

dominance_rules.rule: A frame-qualified estimate band dominates a single national number
dominance_rules.rationale: public data supports within-frame estimates, not a national unit-share or count
dominance_rules.trigger: any request for a single 'how many' or 'what %' figure
dominance_rules.action: deliver the method plus a frame-qualified [ESTIMATE] band and its [UNKNOWN] bucket, never a fabricated point

dominance_rules.rule: The category-by-finish cross dominates either axis alone
dominance_rules.rationale: addressable plated demand lives in specific cells that a one-axis read hides
dominance_rules.trigger: a decision is framed on category demand or finish mix alone
dominance_rules.action: resolve it on the segment-map cell, not the marginal axis

dominance_rules.rule: Purchase confirmation dominates search intent before acting
dominance_rules.rationale: search volume leads and can diverge from realized purchase
dominance_rules.trigger: a subtype is high on search but unconfirmed on purchase
dominance_rules.action: treat it as emerging interest to test, not demand, until a purchase proxy or poll confirms

dominance_rules.rule: A trailing-window read dominates a single-week snapshot for durability claims
dominance_rules.rationale: gifting and viral spikes masquerade as steady demand in a snapshot
dominance_rules.trigger: a subtype is called durable from one capture
dominance_rules.action: require a seasonally-qualified trailing or year-over-year window before labeling demand durable

dominance_rules.rule: Structural fit dominates market-size assertions for the tier choice
dominance_rules.rationale: the venture's plating capability and buyer fit are known while national shares are [UNKNOWN] here
dominance_rules.trigger: the fashion-tier choice is argued from a market-size number
dominance_rules.action: justify the tier on capability/buyer/cost/channel fit and carry the crowding/margin cost to economics

dominance_rules.rule: The [UNKNOWN] bucket dominates a forced finish assignment
dominance_rules.rationale: assigning an unverifiable claim to a finish rung fabricates precision
dominance_rules.trigger: a SKU lacks the base-metal/thickness data to verify its finish
dominance_rules.action: route it to the [UNKNOWN] bucket and report the bucket size rather than guessing a rung

dominance_rules.rule: The tag-and-frame travel with every number at hand-off
dominance_rules.rationale: a stripped estimate reads as a national fact downstream
dominance_rules.trigger: a read is summarized or handed off
dominance_rules.action: keep the [FACT]/[METHOD]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tag and the frame/date attached and refuse promotion to unqualified fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define and document the sampling frame before computing any share or rank
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole assortment/demand read that must be redone because its frame was undefined or unrepresentative

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify finish claims against FTC thresholds before aggregating a finish-mix share
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a solid-vs-plated estimate inflated by marketing words that must be re-tallied after the fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read demand at subtype granularity from the start where the frame exposes it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running the read because a hot subtype was hidden inside a rolled-up top category

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the [ESTIMATE]/frame/date tag to every number at the moment it is produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a frame-qualified band circulating as a national fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute both assortment and demand-weighted finish shares together, not just assortment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reporting a supply-side share as share-of-sales and re-deriving the demand-weighted view later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Seasonally qualify a snapshot and note the window when the read is taken
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a gifting spike being banked as durable demand and reversed after the season turns

anti_rework_rules.rule: State the rhodium facts (wearing thin layer, tarnish-resistant PGM) precisely up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a permanent-shine overclaim that must be corrected against the materials facts and FTC risk

anti_rework_rules.rule: Triangulate with an explicit weighting scheme rather than a hidden blend
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a demand ranking that must be re-justified when its implicit analyst weighting is questioned

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log every deferred quantity (demographics, brands, prices, unit counts) in the unknowns ledger at the boundary
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a downstream specialist filling a deferred [UNKNOWN] with a guess that must later be unwound

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fresh capture window is run or the frame panel changes
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the three proxies, the triangulated ranking and the finish-mix estimate and re-qualify by the new frame/date

iteration_protocol.trigger: the FTC Jewelry Guides amend a finish definition or threshold
iteration_protocol.action: update the FTC definitions, the finish ladder and the verification thresholds and re-run any affected finish classification

iteration_protocol.trigger: a jewel_poll result resolves a split-signal subtype
iteration_protocol.action: update the triangulation confidence flag and the demand ranking tier for that subtype

iteration_protocol.trigger: point-of-sale or panel data becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the solid-vs-plated estimate and the demand ranking from proxy bands toward measured shares, keeping the tags

iteration_protocol.trigger: a seasonal boundary is crossed or a trailing window becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight the demand read for seasonality and re-flag which subtype rankings are durable vs spike-driven

iteration_protocol.trigger: jewel_materials revises the rhodium or finish-durability facts
iteration_protocol.action: update the rhodium positioning and the finish ladder rungs

iteration_protocol.trigger: the [UNKNOWN] finish bucket exceeds an actionable threshold
iteration_protocol.action: run a sampled deep-dive or supplier query to reclassify a subset and re-report the finish-mix band

iteration_protocol.trigger: a downstream specialist (jewel_assortment/jewel_poll/economics) requests a different cut or granularity
iteration_protocol.action: re-cut the demand ranking and segment map at the requested granularity and re-route the hand-off

priority_rationale: The scope/honesty contract, category taxonomy, FTC finish definitions and finish ladder come first because every demand and finish number depends on a fixed classification and the tagging discipline; the sampling frame and the three demand proxies (best-seller rank, search volume, assortment share) next, because they are the public-data instruments; triangulation, the bias ledger, finish-claim verification and the solid-vs-plated estimate then convert those instruments into honest rankings and finish-mix bands; and the demand ranking, segment map, rhodium positioning, seasonality, fashion-tier rationale, unknowns ledger and hand-off come last because they compose the category-and-finish outputs, justify the owner's tier, and route the tagged deliverables while logging what stays [UNKNOWN].
